notes: The direct PDF URL fetched successfully via curl with a browser User-Agent header (HTTP 200, a 3-page PDF) despite the roster's own note that its automated web-text checker had failed on this same URL -- no workaround via the diocesan resource page was needed.

The PDF has no cover page or embedded document title (its own PDF metadata Title field is blank, and the only header text printed on the table is 'Date' / 'Prayer Petition'); it never states its own diocese's full formal name, referring to itself only as 'the Diocese of Ohio' throughout the running text. The `diocese` field ('The Episcopal Diocese of Ohio') is instead taken from the diocesan website's own page title at the resource page dohio.org/the-episcopal-faith/diocesan-cycle-of-prayer ('Diocesan Cycle of Prayer | The Episcopal Diocese of Ohio').

Unlike most other diocese files in this corpus, this source publishes each week as ONE full narrative sentence per date (e.g. 'In the Diocese of Ohio, we pray for X; Y; and Z, and their surrounding communities.') rather than an itemized subject list. All 52 Sundays of 2026 (Jan 4 - Dec 27) are covered, confirmed by rendering all 3 pages as images and visually comparing every row against the extracted text before trusting it -- single-column layout throughout, no interleaving risk.

Every named congregation (always formatted 'Name, Place') is split into its own `parish` subject, one per congregation, the same convention used elsewhere in this corpus for semicolon/comma-separated parish lists.

For non-parish ('category') weeks, this source names its subject(s) inside a full sentence rather than a printed list, requiring a judgment call on how to segment it: each independently-nameable body/group joined by 'and' in the sentence is recorded as its own `category` subject, with its name trimmed of the 'we pray for' lead-in and any trailing 'and their surrounding communities' boilerplate, but otherwise verbatim from the source. A sentence naming ONE class of subject with an internal enumeration of its own members/sub-types (introduced by a colon or 'including', or where splitting would require fabricating a shared prefix/suffix that is not actually printed at the split point, e.g. 'our Companion Dioceses of Belize and Tanga, Tanzania') is instead kept as a single `category` subject, verbatim including its own enumeration.

Additional descriptive context this source states about a specific subject beyond its bare name (e.g. a congregation's closure, an event's own timing) is preserved in that subject's own `note` field rather than folded into `name`, so `name` stays a clean noun phrase while none of the source's stated content is lost: Feb 8 (Church of Our Saviour, Salem and Holy Trinity, Lisbon -- the source states they 'conclude their life as faith communities, with their final services held yesterday'), Feb 15 (St. James, Boardman -- 'their final service, which is being held today'), Mar 22 (Trinity Cathedral, Cleveland -- 'for its ministry as the cathedral church of the diocese'), Jun 7 (Bellwether Farm Summer Camp -- 'as the camp season begins'), Jul 26 (the Big Provincial Gathering -- 'as it prepares to meet this coming week'), Nov 15 (the 210th Diocesan Convention -- 'as it prepares to gather').

Feb 8 and Feb 15's congregations (Church of Our Saviour/Salem, Holy Trinity/Lisbon, St. James/Boardman) are transcribed as ordinary `parish` subjects since the source itself still names them as congregations of the diocese being prayed for on these dates, notwithstanding their announced closures.

Jun 28's 'St. Andrew Church, Mentor' is printed without the possessive apostrophe-s that every other 'St. Andrew' congregation in this source carries (e.g. 'St. Andrew's Church, Elyria', 'St. Andrew's Church, Cleveland', 'St. Andrew's Church, Toledo') -- preserved verbatim per this corpus's standing rule against silently correcting a diocese's own published document.

Oct 11's entry reads 'we give thanks and pray for Bishop Anne B. Jolly and the diocesan staff' -- the only week using 'give thanks and pray for' rather than this source's usual 'we pray for'; preserved as printed, not treated as an error.

Dec 27's petition itself names 'the Diocese of Southern Ohio' as a prayer subject, alongside neighboring dioceses in Indiana, Michigan, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia. This is the source's own content and refers to a distinct diocese (Southern Ohio) from the Diocese of Ohio being transcribed in this file (dioceseShort 'ohio') -- the two are not the same diocese and are not to be confused.
No liturgical Sunday names or season labels (e.g. 'Proper 15', 'Advent') are printed anywhere in this source -- `liturgicalNote` is null on every entry.
